title: Keep Your Receipts: Trustworthy Cleanup of Agent-Built Knowledge Graphs

object.carrier: agent-built knowledge graph over source documents (extracted claims, entity merges, schema-entailed edges, community summaries), where every artifact carries a support-label receipt: alternative bundles of source assertions each claimed sufficient on its own

safety_property.statement: When a source is retracted or a predicate revoked, the persisted agent-built graph must stop serving artifacts that no longer re-derive from surviving evidence (no leakage of invalidated content) while retaining artifacts a surviving derivation still supports (no over-deletion). The property fails silently when the model's own receipts wrongly claim an artifact still stands.
safety_property.operationalized_as: label faithfulness graded against a re-derivation oracle (agreement / leaky / over-deleted rates per layer, Tables 2-3), and retrieval-level exposure as tainted@10 with recall@10 against a deployed-deletion baseline (Table 4)

capabilities: the constructor LLM authors its own receipts (self-reports), which can be leaky: claiming an artifact survives a deletion when re-derivation says it is dead
the constructor samples, so rebuilding is noisy and cannot serve as a verifier
non-adversarial harness faults also corrupt the artifact store (provider banner / refusals cached as model answers)
assumptions: no deliberate adversary; the untrusted party is the model's unreliable self-report, not an attacker
receipts are demanded in the same model call that creates the artifact; no later process can recover them
liveness is graded by re-derivation with R=5 independent draws per touched artifact at threshold tau=0.2, matching the stochastic constructor
entailed edges are re-derived symbolically and agree by construction
not_covered: adversarial attacks such as prompt injection or deliberate poisoning of receipts
source-groundedness: artifacts the model regenerates from parametric memory grade alive without surviving source support (matters for right-to-erasure)
additions/updates to the graph (only deletion is studied)
consumers that reason over retrieval paths rather than top-k keyword retrieval
failures in the harness/cache layer, which no audit of the model's reasoning sees (Section 7 incident)

intervention.name: PolyGraph: receipt-and-audit protocol with a layered trust policy
intervention.description: The constructor must emit, in the same call that creates an artifact, a support label: alternative bundles of source assertions, each claimed sufficient on its own. Cleanup of a withdrawal is then set arithmetic over the receipts (milliseconds on the whole graph, no model calls). Because receipts are model self-reports, a re-derivation audit grades them by deleting the cited evidence and testing whether the constructor still produces the artifact (R=5 draws, tau=0.2). The audit's layer-dependent verdict is acted on by a layered policy: trust merge and entailed-edge labels, distrust flat summary labels and remove touched summaries; sentence-level receipts repair the summary layer.

results.claim: In this corpus, the deployed policy of deleting only directly extracted facts barely cleans the graph under a real retraction and does nothing under predicate revocation, because the damage sits in derived edges and summaries.
results.setting: 300 PubMed oncology abstracts (61 genuinely retracted), Claude Sonnet constructor, BM25 retrieval over MeSH-descriptor queries
results.quote: On our corpus that reduces contaminated queries from 32.2% to 28.0% under a real retraction and leaves predicate revocation unchanged at 36.8%.
results.locator: Abstract; see also Section 1 and Table 4

denominator.how_counted: Table 4: BM25, k=10, 300 MeSH-descriptor queries; truth is the re-derivation oracle

results.claim: On this stochastic constructor, rebuilding the graph cannot stand in for verification: two builds of the unchanged corpus differ in about five times as many artifacts as removing the retracted documents changes.
results.value: resampling floor 29,475 vs deletion effect 6,248 artifacts
results.setting: two independent builds of the same 300-document corpus vs a build omitting the 61 retracted documents, Claude Sonnet constructor
results.quote: Rerunning the constructor on unchanged input changes 29,475 artifacts. Removing the retracted documents changes 6,248.

denominator.how_counted: Table 1: symmetric difference between two independent builds (floor) and between full and retracted builds (effect)

results.claim: Self-reported receipts are trustworthy at the merge layer but not at the summary layer as originally elicited: the same agent in the same pipeline can be trusted about entity merges and not about its flat-summary receipts.
results.setting: full populations of touched model-authored artifacts under retract-source and revoke-relation, re-derivation oracle R=5, tau=0.2, Claude Sonnet constructor, biomedical graph
results.quote: Merge labels agree with re-derivation 68.4% and 84.6% of the time; summary labels, 33.3% and 36.4%.

denominator.n_total: 21 touched merges and 7 touched summaries under retract-source; 29 merges and 25 summaries under revoke-relation (populations, not samples)
denominator.how_counted: Table 2: every model-authored artifact the deletion touched was adjudicated; undecided artifacts counted separately

results.claim: The summary layer's failure is traced to receipt shape and repaired: eliciting one receipt per sentence makes summary receipts as faithful as the merge layer's, with errors no longer one-sided.
results.value: 100% and 87.6% agreement; 4.1% leaky vs 8.3% over-deleted under revoke-relation
results.setting: same 59 communities, same deletions and re-derivation oracle (R=5, tau=0.2), sentence-level receipt elicitation vs the pipeline's original flat format
results.quote: Audited sentence by sentence, these receipts agree with re-derivation 100% and 87.6% of the time, the merge layer's range, and their errors are no longer one-sided (4.1% leaky against 8.3% over-deleted under revoke-relation).

denominator.n_total: 62 and 124 touched sentences audited as their own artifacts
denominator.how_counted: Table 3: sentence-level rows audit each touched sentence as its own artifact, so n counts sentences

results.claim: Acting on the audit verdict (distrust the failing summary layer) cuts contaminated queries to below one percent at identical recall with no additional model calls.
results.setting: BM25, k=10, 300 MeSH-descriptor queries, truth = re-derivation oracle, biomedical graph
results.quote: Trusting all labels already reduces contamination from the deployed baseline's 28.0% and 36.8% of queries to 0.8% and 2.1%. Applying the verdict halves the remainder, to 0.4% and 0.8%, at identical recall and no additional model calls.

denominator.how_counted: Table 4: BM25, k=10, 300 MeSH-descriptor queries; truth is the re-derivation oracle

results.claim: The layer ordering holds when populations grow: pooled over ten further random retractions, summary receipts leak far more often than merge receipts, with summary over-deletion at zero in every deletion.
results.setting: ten further random 10% retractions of the biomedical graph, same protocol, pooled (deletion, artifact) adjudications
results.quote: On 238 decided merges and 109 decided summaries the gap stands on its own: merges 18.1% leaky [13.7, 23.5], summaries 41.3% leaky [32.5, 50.7], with summary over-deletion at zero in every deletion.

denominator.how_counted: Section 6.3: pooled every (deletion, artifact) adjudication over ten further random 10% retractions; undecided excluded

results.claim: On a second domain (Supreme Court opinions) with the policy fixed in advance, the layer ordering and the layered policy's benefit carry over: distrusting the summary layer removes all measured contamination while keeping recall.
results.setting: 150 U.S. Supreme Court opinions graph (same pipeline, legal schema), merge receipts 80.0%/76.2% and summary receipts 43.8%/12.5% agreement with re-derivation, random-document retract-source
results.quote: merge receipts agree with re-derivation 80.0% and 76.2% of the time, summary receipts 43.8% and 12.5%, every summary error a leak, and distrusting the summary layer brings contamination from 15.7% and 4.7% to 0.0% at 99.9% and 100% recall.

denominator.how_counted: Section 3: the Supreme Court corpus's queries are 300 party and citation strings

results.claim: 撤销（withdrawal）操作本身是集合运算，在 24,381 个 artifact 的图上耗时 1–21 ms，即撤销开销可计量且很小。
results.comparison: no model calls (零模型调用) vs 需要重新推导的清理策略
results.setting: 24,381-artifact 知识图；带 receipt 的清理管线；全程本地
results.quote: Cleanup then needs no model calls, because the information that removal requires was stored before it was needed; processing a withdrawal is set arithmetic over the receipts, 1 to 21 ms on our whole 24,381-artifact graph.
results.locator: Section on receipt-based cleanup (cleanup cost paragraph)

limitations.statement: The audit measures constructor-relative liveness, not source-groundedness: an artifact the model can regenerate from parametric memory grades alive even if no surviving source supports it, which is the failure that matters most for right-to-erasure.
limitations.quote: Re-derivation asks the constructor that built the graph, so an artifact the model can regenerate from parametric memory grades alive even if no surviving source supports it.

limitations.statement: The size of the summary layer's leakage is setting-specific (varies widely across constructor, corpus and operation), so the layered policy's margin over trusting all labels does not generalize; both constructors are Claude models, corpora are small, and behavior at larger scale is unmeasured.
limitations.quote: the size of the summary layer's leakage did not, ranging from 8% to 88% across constructor, corpus and operation, so the layered policy's margin over trusting all labels is setting-specific.

limitations.statement: The retrieval-level stakes are measured with a keyword BM25 retriever over single queries; a consumer that reasons over paths can be contaminated by a dead edge it never retrieves directly.
limitations.quote: A consumer that reasons over paths meets every artifact on the path, so one dead edge can contaminate an answer that never retrieves the edge directly.

limitations.statement: Only deletion is studied; when a still-alive summary has become incomplete and should be regenerated is a design question the authors have not studied.
limitations.quote: What additions do not settle is when a still-alive summary has become incomplete and should be regenerated; that is a design question for the constructor, and we have not studied it.

limitations.statement: The verdict granularity is coarse: five re-derivation draws at tau=0.2 leave artifacts near the threshold in an undecided band that is excluded from scoring.
limitations.quote: artifacts near the threshold land in the undecided band (2 to 3 per cell) and are excluded.
